subject: Cloud affinity shift: immediate customer traffic guidance and post-incident follow-up
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-07T07:12:00-07:00
Subject: Cloud affinity shift: immediate customer traffic guidance and post-incident follow-up

Hi Samantha —

Quick update from our side: this morning at ~07:00 PDT we observed an acute peering/affinity disruption in the primary cloud region servicing AcmeCloud (affecting both eu-west and us-central paths), which caused degraded throughput for some requests and intermittent 5xx errors. Our infra team applied an affinity-shift policy to route new sessions to the secondary ILB endpoints and initiated cross-region warmups to reduce cold-starts.

What we want you to do right now:
- Update your endpoint affinity header to prefer the fallback region for 30m (examples attached).
- If you run long-lived connections, proactively reconnect after 07:20 PDT to pick up the warmed routing.
- Watch for increased latency for embeddings / long-generation requests and temporarily reduce max_tokens to avoid timeouts.

Attachments: affinity-shift-instructions-v1.pdf (step-by-step endpoint examples), customer-traffic-checklist.csv (quick checklist).

We'll keep you posted with a short postmortem and timeline once we validate the change lasted. Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts production traffic and we're prioritizing a durable fix.

Best,
Irene
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Lee <samantha@acmecloud.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-07T07:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cloud affinity shift: immediate customer traffic guidance and post-incident follow-up

Thanks, Irene —

We applied the affinity header change across our fleets at 07:35 PDT. Two quick questions:
1) Do you have guidance for how long we should preserve the fallback preference before switching back to original affinity?
2) Will any tokens or usage be doubled/charged differently during the reconnect window?

I tried the short checklist; a couple of internal teams reported reconnects succeeded but we saw a brief spike in token timeouts.

— Sam
Platform Ops, AcmeCloud

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@acmecloud.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-07T08:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cloud affinity shift: immediate customer traffic guidance and post-incident follow-up

On Jun 7, 2028, Samantha Lee wrote: > We applied the affinity header change ...

Sam —
Short answers:
- Maintain the fallback preference for 30–60 minutes after traffic normalizes. We'll post a follow-up "all-clear" message once cache hit rates and p95 latency stabilize for 15 consecutive minutes.
- Token accounting: there is no duplication of billing tokens from our side for retries; normal token counts apply. However, if your client retried requests client-side, that could increase usage — the checklist recommends setting idempotent retries and short jitter windows.

Technical note: the affinity policy we pushed keeps warm K/V caches in the secondary region for 45 minutes; you should only see increased latency (not degraded model outputs) during the first few reconnections while KV warming finishes.

I'll keep monitoring and will post metrics in this thread.

Thanks,
Marcus
Sr. Reliability Engineer

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-07T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: customer comms checklist and escalation notes

Team —
Internal checklist completed and next steps:

- Product: Vanessa to coordinate any SLAs impacted and determine if an SLA credit conversation is needed (tag: PLG accounts).
- CS: Irene to send a post-incident summary and schedule a 30-minute review with AcmeCloud tomorrow.

I've attached the customer-traffic-checklist.csv for reference. Leave comments in the incident doc (DOCID-79823).

Laura
Head of Support Operations

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@acmecloud.com>, Timothy Ng <timothy@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-08T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary and scheduled review: affinity disruption (June 7)

Hi Sam / Tim —

Thanks again for cooperating during the affinity shift. We've completed our initial internal investigation and confirmed the following:
- Root cause: an automated peering policy rollback at the cloud provider triggered an unanticipated affinity imbalance for sessions originating from select edge PoPs.
- Impact window: 2028-06-07T06:58:00Z through 2028-06-07T08:05:00Z (approx).
- Customer-visible effects: brief p95 latency increases (~1200ms peak) and intermittent 500 errors for long generation requests.

Mitigation executed: affinity-shift policy to route new sessions to warmed secondary ILBs, warmup scripts for KV caches, and temporary client guidance to reconnect.

Action items (owners / ETA):
- Engineering (Marcus): permanent affinity-health checks + autoswitch on unhealthy PoPs (proposal by 2028-06-14).
- Product (Vanessa): consider adding a self-service affinity-preference toggle in Console (scoping by 2028-06-21).
- CS (Irene): 1:1 review with AcmeCloud scheduled for 2028-06-09T11:00 PDT (calendar invite sent).

We'll follow up after the review with a detailed root-cause postmortem and timeline. Let us know if you'd like immediate access to logs or a short dashboard walk-through.

Regards,
Irene

From: Samantha Lee <samantha@acmecloud.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Cc: Timoth y Ng <timothy@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2028-06-10T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident summary and scheduled review: affinity disruption (June 7)

Appreciate the summary, Irene. The 1:1 went well yesterday — we validated the warmup behavior and our teams agreed the 30–60 minute fallback recommendation works operationally. Two asks from AcmeCloud:
1) Can Redwood provide a short runbook snippet we can import into our incident playbooks (YAML or markdown)?
2) We saw one customer-side retry that created extra load while our clients were reconnecting — is there a recommended client retry policy you can share that balances reliability and rate-safety?

If you can drop those two items into the shared doc (DOCID-79823), we'll close the loop.

— Sam
